papers.title: Large Language Models as a Universal Searcher for Open-World Automated Machine Learning
papers.abstract_en: Developing effective machine learning models requires complex manual tuning, while current Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) frameworks remain domain-specific and isolate model architecture, training hyperparameter, and data ratio optimization. Here, we bridge this gap by proposing a universal, large language model (LLM)-based AutoML framework that jointly optimizes these configurations for the first time without the need for task-specific fine-tuning. We propose NCode, a unified numerical encoding scheme that translates diverse AutoML design choices into universal discrete sequences and effectively reframes the optimization process as a unified ranking task. Trained solely on optimization trajectories derived from a limited, single-domain vision task, the proposed LLM-based searcher demonstrates impressive cross-task, cross-modality and joint search-space optimization generalizability, achieving state-of-the-art performance across image classification, image segmentation, speaker verification and text-to-image benchmarks. Crucially, it exhibits superior scalability in the large-scale training and joint optimization of a billion-parameter Diffusion Transformer, requiring 896 GPU-days and attaining a state-of-the-art GenEval score of 0.91. By leveraging reinforcement learning to instill Chain-of-Thought reasoning, we provide a systematic way to interpret the LLM-based searcher's internal decision-making mechanisms, revealing its optimization strategy shifted from the early-stage diversity-driven exploration to the late-stage anchor exploitation. Our proposed framework provides a scalable, generalizable, and interpretable pathway toward general-purpose open-world machine learning optimization.
papers.abstract_zh: 开发有效的机器学习模型需要复杂的人工调优，而当前的自动化机器学习（AutoML）框架仍局限于特定领域，并将模型架构、训练超参数和数据比例优化相互隔离。在此，我们通过提出一个通用的、基于大语言模型（LLM）的AutoML框架来弥合这一差距，该框架首次联合优化这些配置，且无需任务特定微调。我们提出NCode，一种统一的数值编码方案，将多样的AutoML设计选择转化为通用离散序列，并有效地将优化过程重构为统一排序任务。所提出的基于LLM的搜索器仅在一个有限单领域视觉任务的优化轨迹上训练，却展现出令人印象深刻的跨任务、跨模态和联合搜索空间优化泛化能力，在图像分类、图像分割、说话人验证和文本到图像基准上取得最先进性能。关键的是，它在十亿参数扩散Transformer的大规模训练和联合优化中展现出优越的可扩展性，需要896 GPU天并达到0.91的最先进GenEval分数。通过利用强化学习灌输思维链推理，我们提供了一种系统化方式来解释基于LLM的搜索器的内部决策机制，揭示其优化策略从早期多样性驱动的探索转向后期锚点利用。我们提出的框架为通用开放世界机器学习优化提供了一条可扩展、可泛化且可解释的路径。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出基于LLM的通用AutoML框架NCode，将架构、超参数与数据比例选择统一编码为排序任务，仅用单领域视觉轨迹训练即实现跨任务跨模态泛化，并在十亿参数扩散Transformer联合优化中达到0.91 GenEval分数。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model, transformer
匹配 模型架构：model architecture
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: PORT: Preference Optimization via Robust Token-Level Reweighting
papers.abstract_en: Preference optimization has become a central approach for aligning large language models with human values, but its effectiveness depends heavily on the quality of preference annotations. In practice, preference data is often noisy due to annotation errors and ambiguity. Existing robust preference optimization methods primarily operate at the sequence level, implicitly treating entire responses as uniformly correct or incorrect. However, rejected responses may still contain informative reasoning steps, while preferred responses can include subtle errors. In this work, we propose \textbf{P}reference \textbf{O}ptimization via \textbf{R}obust \textbf{T}oken-level reweighting \textbf{(PORT)}, a fine-grained framework for robust alignment under noisy preferences. PORT performs token-level reweighting using the empirical cumulative distribution function (CDF) of token log-probabilities, yielding an efficient forward-pass-only proxy to gradient-norm penalization that selectively suppresses corrupted tokens without additional backward-pass computation. We provide theoretical analysis showing that PORT reduces the gradient bias from noisy preference labels by minimizing an upper bound on the bias term. Extensive experiments across diverse noise settings demonstrate that PORT consistently improves robustness and outperforms existing sequence-level baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/osu-srml/PORT
papers.abstract_zh: 偏好优化已成为使大语言模型与人类价值对齐的核心方法，但其有效性在很大程度上取决于偏好标注的质量。在实践中，由于标注错误和歧义，偏好数据往往带有噪声。现有的鲁棒偏好优化方法主要在序列级操作，隐含地将整个回复视为统一正确或错误。然而，被拒绝的回复仍可能包含有信息量的推理步骤，而被偏好的回复也可能包含细微错误。在本工作中，我们提出通过鲁棒 token 级重加权进行偏好优化（PORT），一种在噪声偏好下进行鲁棒对齐的细粒度框架。PORT利用 token 对数概率的经验累积分布函数（CDF）进行 token 级重加权，产生一种仅需前向传播的高效梯度范数惩罚代理，在不增加反向传播计算的情况下选择性抑制损坏的 token。我们提供理论分析，表明PORT通过最小化偏差项的上界来减少噪声偏好标签带来的梯度偏差。跨多种噪声设置的广泛实验表明，PORT持续提升鲁棒性并优于现有序列级基线。代码见 https://github.com/osu-srml/PORT。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出PORT框架，利用token对数概率的经验CDF进行token级重加权，以仅前向传播的方式选择性抑制噪声偏好中的损坏token，理论证明其降低梯度偏差并在多种噪声设置下优于序列级基线。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model
匹配 预训练 / 后训练：preference optimization
evidence: 实验或理论证据信号：extensive experiment, theoretical analysis
开放资源信号：code is available

papers.title: TMT: Adapting CLIP to Infrared Imagery via Text-Derived Modality Knowledge Transfer
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language models such as CLIP achieve strong performance across computer vision tasks, yet their image-text alignment is less reliable for infrared (IR) imagery because large-scale pre-training is dominated by visible-spectrum data. Due to the high cost of the infrared-text labeling, we investigate adapting CLIP to IR through only paired infrared-visible images, which requires considering modality-specific knowledge while preserving scene content and CLIP's image-text alignment. To achieve this, we propose TMT (Text-Derived Modality Knowledge Transfer), which adapts CLIP's image encoder through a text-defined infrared-to-visible direction and supervision from paired IR-visible images. First, we found that modality discrepancy can be described by corresponding text embeddings, thus using the direction of text embedding differences to guide the knowledge transfer between visible and infrared modalities without erasing infrared-specific information. To enhance the representation of semantics and details of infrared images, we introduce Generative-Perceptual Co-Supervision that combines semantic alignment from CLIP visible image encoder with diffusion noise-prediction feedbacks. On four source-disjoint IR classification benchmarks, TMT achieves the highest mean zero-shot accuracy among the compared methods (48.92%). It also achieves the best IR-text retrieval results among the compared methods without infrared-text supervision during adaptation and the highest open-vocabulary segmentation mIoU on both CART and SemanticRT among the CLIP-like methods.
papers.abstract_zh: CLIP等视觉-语言模型在各类计算机视觉任务中表现强劲，但由于大规模预训练以可见光数据为主，其图像-文本对齐对红外（IR）图像不够可靠。鉴于红外-文本标注成本高昂，我们研究仅通过成对的红外-可见光图像将CLIP适配到红外模态，这需要在保留场景内容和CLIP图像-文本对齐的同时考虑模态特定知识。为此，我们提出TMT（文本导出的模态知识迁移），通过文本定义的红外到可见光方向以及成对红外-可见光图像的监督来适配CLIP的图像编码器。首先，我们发现模态差异可由对应的文本嵌入描述，因此利用文本嵌入差异的方向引导可见光与红外模态间的知识迁移，而不抹除红外特有信息。为增强红外图像语义与细节的表示，我们引入生成-感知协同监督，结合来自CLIP可见光图像编码器的语义对齐与扩散噪声预测反馈。在四个源不相交的红外分类基准上，TMT在对比方法中取得最高平均零样本准确率（48.92%）。在适配期间无红外-文本监督的情况下，它也在对比方法中取得最佳红外-文本检索结果，并在CLIP类方法中于CART和SemanticRT上取得最高开放词汇分割mIoU。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出TMT，利用文本嵌入差异方向与成对红外-可见光图像监督将CLIP适配到红外模态，在四个红外分类基准上取得48.92%的平均零样本准确率。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pre-training
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Understanding Mixture-of-Experts Language Models Beyond Expert Boundaries
papers.abstract_en: In Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, the nature of expert specialization remains controversial. Reports of domain-associated expert preferences contrast with analyses attributing routing primarily to token identity or syntactic patterns. To clarify these differing accounts, we look beyond expert-level routing to investigate the neuron-level organization of domain-specialized computation using Routing-Aware Magnitude Profiling (RAMP), a measure developed for this analysis. Using mixed-domain calibration data, we identify domain-specialized neuron sets with 58-74% overlap across multi-source samples of the same domain, compared with 15-24% across domains. To understand how this organization evolves during training, we trace neuron importance throughout pre-training and post-training across three fully open MoE families. Neuron importance continues to reorganize between pre-training checkpoints despite comparatively stable expert-level importance rankings, while post-training largely preserves neuron rankings. Building on these neuron-level perspectives, we further introduce RAMP-based Pruning (RAMPr) to select neurons across experts for balanced multi-domain capability preservation. At 75% neuron retention, RAMPr preserves average 91-98% of original full performance across six models. At 50% retention, our pruning method can reduce resident GPU memory by 36-43% and improves batched prefill throughput by 17-39% effectively. Our code is available at https://github.com/ydyjya/Neuron-Level-Specialization-in-MoE
papers.abstract_zh: 在混合专家（MoE）模型中，专家专门化的本质仍存在争议。关于专家偏好与领域相关的报告，与将路由主要归因于token身份或句法模式的分析形成对比。为厘清这些不同解释，我们超越专家级路由，利用为分析开发的Routing-Aware Magnitude Profiling（RAMP）度量，研究领域专门化计算在神经元层面的组织。使用混合领域校准数据，我们识别出领域专门化神经元集合，同一领域多源样本间的重叠率为58-74%，而跨领域重叠率为15-24%。为理解这种组织在训练中如何演变，我们在三个完全开放的MoE系列中追踪预训练和后训练期间的神经元重要性。尽管专家级重要性排名相对稳定，神经元重要性在预训练检查点之间持续重组，而后训练基本保持神经元排名。基于这些神经元层面视角，我们进一步引入基于RAMP的剪枝（RAMPr），跨专家选择神经元以平衡多领域能力保持。在75%神经元保留率下，RAMPr在六个模型上平均保留原始完整性能的91-98%。在50%保留率下，我们的剪枝方法可将常驻GPU内存减少36-43%，并将批量预填充吞吐量有效提升17-39%。我们的代码见https://github.com/ydyjya/Neuron-Level-Specialization-in-MoE。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出RAMP度量揭示MoE模型领域专门化计算在神经元层面的组织及其训练演变，并据此设计RAMPr剪枝方法，在保留多领域能力的同时降低显存并提升吞吐。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pre-training, post-training
evidence: 开放资源信号：code is available
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: GHiML: VLM-Guided Hierarchical Multi-Label Learning with Applications to Benthic Imagery
papers.abstract_en: Vision language models (VLMs) encode substantial expert knowledge within their weights, yet their direct application to specialised classification domains such as benthic imagery remains limited. Meanwhile, vision transformers trained on these tasks rely predominantly on low-level visual latents (colours, textures, and shapes) that lack the higher-level reasoning humans employ for identification. We propose Guided Hierarchical Multi-Label (GHiML) learning, a pipeline that extracts conceptual latent variables from a VLM conditioned on training data, generates sample-relevant captions grounded in those variables, and fuses the resulting textual embeddings with image embeddings via cross-attention and a per-node gated router. We also introduce the inverted HML score ($d_{\mathrm{inv}}$), a similarity score that evaluates hierarchical multi-label predictions through graph traversal distance and a cardinality penalty, providing an interpretable alternative to existing measures, which are insensitive to realistic degradations in sparse, deep hierarchies. Experiments on BenthicNet, FathomNet and iNaturalist show that the router improves macro $F_1$ over the vision-only baseline by up to 6.7 pp and $d_{\mathrm{inv}}$ by up to 21.1 pp on in-domain benthic data, with gains persisting under distribution shift. Ablations locate the contribution of the text itself: on the multi-label biotic hierarchies, removing the per-sample text signal degrades $d_{\mathrm{inv}}$ while leaving macro $F_1$ unchanged, consistent with text acting through prediction cardinality rather than node discrimination, whereas iNaturalist, whose annotations are single-label, loses 18.7% of macro $F_1$. Our results support the hypothesis that VLMs contain exploitable specialised knowledge that, when appropriately elicited, can augment classification in domains where direct visual learning is insufficient.
papers.abstract_zh: 视觉语言模型（VLM）在其权重中编码了大量专家知识，但其在底栖图像等专业分类领域的直接应用仍然有限。与此同时，在这些任务上训练的视觉Transformer主要依赖低级视觉潜变量（颜色、纹理和形状），缺乏人类用于识别的高层推理。我们提出引导式层次多标签（GHiML）学习，这是一条流水线：以训练数据为条件从VLM中提取概念潜变量，生成基于这些变量的样本相关描述，并通过交叉注意力和逐节点门控路由器将所得文本嵌入与图像嵌入融合。我们还引入倒置HML分数（$d_{\mathrm{inv}}$），一种通过图遍历距离和基数惩罚评估层次多标签预测的相似度分数，为现有度量（对稀疏、深层层次结构中现实退化不敏感）提供可解释的替代方案。在BenthicNet、FathomNet和iNaturalist上的实验表明，该路由器在域内底栖数据上将宏$F_1$较纯视觉基线提升最多6.7个百分点，将$d_{\mathrm{inv}}$提升最多21.1个百分点，且在分布偏移下增益持续存在。消融实验定位了文本本身的贡献：在多标签生物层次结构上，移除逐样本文本信号会降低$d_{\mathrm{inv}}$而宏$F_1$不变，这与文本通过预测基数而非节点判别起作用的结论一致；而标注为单标签的iNaturalist则损失18.7%的宏$F_1$。我们的结果支持如下假设：VLM包含可被利用的专业知识，在适当引出后能够增强直接视觉学习不足领域的分类。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出GHiML，从VLM提取概念潜变量生成描述并与图像嵌入融合，在底栖数据上宏F1最高提升6.7个百分点，并引入倒置HML分数$d_{\mathrm{inv}}$。
why_it_matters: 匹配 MLLM / VLM：vision language model, vlm
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: TimeSeek: Multi-Task and Multi-Domain Pretraining for Generalized Time Series Analytics
papers.abstract_en: Time series analytics has been widely applied across various domains. While existing time series foundation models (TSFMs) have demonstrated promising results, they still face two major challenges: 1) Most TSFMs mainly rely on stacking Transformer layers to increase parameter size, lacking the ability to adaptively model complex time series patterns from multi-domain data. 2) Current TSFMs are primarily pre-trained for specific tasks, e.g., forecasting or anomaly detection, and a few models support multiple tasks, but they fail to fully leverage task specificity and commonality, resulting in suboptimal performance. To address these challenges, we propose TimeSeek, a novel generalized time series analytics model that adaptively models time series patterns from multi-domain data and unifies multiple tasks in pre-training. Conceptually, TimeSeek is guided by selective information sharing under domain and task heterogeneity. From the perspective of multi-domain data, we propose a Multi-Domain Feature Extractor that adaptively captures temporal dependencies and channel correlations based on domain-specific characteristics, including progressive multi-scale modeling and adaptive slot channel modeling. From the perspective of the diversity of tasks, we propose multi-task collaborative training, which leverages task specificity and task commonality through task customization and cross-task training, effectively unifying multiple tasks in pre-training and better adapting to diverse downstream scenarios. After pre-training on large-scale time series data, TimeSeek achieves state-of-the-art performance in forecasting, anomaly detection, and classification tasks across both few-shot learning and zero-shot situations, together with favorable inference efficiency.
papers.abstract_zh: 时间序列分析已广泛应用于各个领域。尽管现有时间序列基础模型（TSFM）已展现出良好结果，但仍面临两大挑战：1）大多数TSFM主要依赖堆叠Transformer层来增加参数量，缺乏从多领域数据自适应建模复杂时间序列模式的能力。2）当前TSFM主要针对特定任务（如预测或异常检测）预训练，少数模型支持多任务，但未能充分利用任务特异性和共性，导致性能次优。为应对这些挑战，我们提出TimeSeek，一种新颖的广义时间序列分析模型，可从多领域数据自适应建模时间序列模式并在预训练中统一多任务。在概念上，TimeSeek以领域和任务异质性下的选择性信息共享为指导。从多领域数据角度，我们提出多领域特征提取器，基于领域特定特性自适应捕获时间依赖和通道相关性，包括渐进多尺度建模和自适应槽通道建模。从任务多样性角度，我们提出多任务协同训练，通过任务定制和跨任务训练利用任务特异性和任务共性，在预训练中有效统一多任务并更好适应多样下游场景。在大规模时间序列数据上预训练后，TimeSeek在少样本和零样本情况下的预测、异常检测和分类任务上均达到最先进性能，并具有良好推理效率。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出TimeSeek，通过多领域特征提取器与多任务协同训练在预训练中统一多任务，在预测、异常检测和分类的少样本与零样本场景下取得最先进性能。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pretraining, pre-training
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Multimodal Road Closure Mapping via Cross-Modal Graph Attention
papers.abstract_en: Accurate and timely identification of road closures is critical for large-scale navigation and logistics systems, yet remains challenging due to the need to jointly reason over visual evidence, spatial context, and road network topology. Existing approaches either rely on manual map updates or focus on detecting closure-related objects without resolving which road segment is affected. In this work, we introduce a unified multimodal and multitask framework that jointly performs road closure classification (no, partial, complete) and road segment association within a single learning architecture. Our model integrates graph-structured map data, satellite imagery augmented with projected street-level detections, and street-view images using modality-specific encoders and cross-modal transformer attention, enabling explicit reasoning over visual cues and network topology. Evaluated on nearly 20K real-world scenarios collected from a large-scale commercial vehicle fleet, our approach achieves 72.7% closure classification accuracy and 60% road segment association accuracy, outperforming frontier vision-language models by over 28 percentage points on closure classification while being over 4,000x smaller and 100x faster at inference. Extensive ablations demonstrate the importance of cross-modal attention, edge-aware pooling, and graph message passing for accurate geospatial reasoning. This work establishes the first benchmark for joint road closure classification and segment-level attribution, and shows that task-specific architectural inductive biases substantially outperform general-purpose multimodal models for structured geospatial understanding.
papers.abstract_zh: 准确及时地识别道路封闭对大规模导航和物流系统至关重要，但由于需要联合推理视觉证据、空间上下文和路网拓扑，仍具挑战性。现有方法要么依赖人工地图更新，要么专注于检测封闭相关对象而未确定受影响的路段。在本工作中，我们引入一个统一的多模态多任务框架，在单一学习架构中联合执行道路封闭分类（无、部分、完全）和路段关联。我们的模型使用模态特定编码器和跨模态Transformer注意力，整合图结构地图数据、增强有投影街景检测的卫星影像以及街景图像，从而对视觉线索和网络拓扑进行显式推理。在从大规模商用车队收集的近2万个真实场景上评估，我们的方法达到72.7%的封闭分类准确率和60%的路段关联准确率，在封闭分类上比前沿视觉语言模型高出超过28个百分点，同时模型小4000倍以上且推理快100倍。大量消融实验表明跨模态注意力、边感知池化和图消息传递对准确地理空间推理的重要性。本工作建立了联合道路封闭分类和路段级归因的首个基准，并表明任务特定的架构归纳偏置在结构化地理空间理解上显著优于通用多模态模型。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出统一多模态多任务框架，结合图结构地图、卫星影像与街景图像及跨模态注意力，联合进行道路封闭分类与路段关联，在真实场景中显著优于前沿视觉语言模型。
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: ScaleBrain: A Scale-Consistent Framework for EEG Foundation Models
papers.abstract_en: Foundation models pre-trained on large unlabeled electroencephalography (EEG) corpora have emerged as a transformative paradigm for Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) applications. Recent EEG foundation models have shown that multi-scale representations derived from fixed-length patches can improve EEG representation learning. Existing frameworks commonly construct temporal scales through feature-level operations. However, these operations leave the correspondence between learned features and scale-specific characteristics of the original EEG signals implicit. Moreover, when the self-supervised objective is not aligned with the multi-scale input representations, information at some temporal scales may receive insufficient supervision during pre-training. In light of this, we propose ScaleBrain, a scale-consistent pre-training framework that explicitly coordinates multi-scale representations of EEG from both the model input and optimization objective sides. Specifically, ScaleBrain introduces multi-scale EEG tokenization to represent the same EEG segment through analysis windows with different temporal spans and shared temporal anchors, and pairs these representations with scale-specific reconstruction to align with the multi-scale input structure and provide supervision across temporal resolutions during self-supervised learning. We further develop an axial spatio-temporal attention mechanism to contextualize the fused multi-scale representation along spatial and temporal dimensions. Extensive evaluations on six public BCI benchmarks against 12 representative baselines show that ScaleBrain achieves the highest mean Balanced Accuracy on five datasets and ranks third on the remaining one, with only 5.0M parameters, demonstrating strong performance and favorable parameter efficiency.
papers.abstract_zh: 在大规模无标签脑电图（EEG）语料上预训练的基础模型已成为脑机接口（BCI）应用的变革性范式。近期EEG基础模型表明，源自固定长度分块的多尺度表示可改善EEG表示学习。现有框架通常通过特征级操作构建时间尺度。然而，这些操作使学习到的特征与原始EEG信号的尺度特定特性之间的对应关系保持隐式。此外，当自监督目标与多尺度输入表示不对齐时，某些时间尺度的信息在预训练期间可能获得不足的监督。鉴于此，我们提出ScaleBrain，一种尺度一致的预训练框架，从模型输入和优化目标两方面显式协调EEG的多尺度表示。具体而言，ScaleBrain引入多尺度EEG分词，通过具有不同时间跨度和共享时间锚点的分析窗口表示同一EEG片段，并将这些表示与尺度特定重建配对，以对齐多尺度输入结构并在自监督学习期间跨时间分辨率提供监督。我们进一步开发轴向时空注意力机制，沿空间和时间维度对融合的多尺度表示进行上下文化。在六个公开BCI基准上与12个代表性基线进行广泛评估，结果表明ScaleBrain在五个数据集上取得最高平均平衡准确率，在其余一个上排名第三，且仅有5.0M参数，展现出强性能和良好的参数效率。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出ScaleBrain，从输入分词与重建目标两侧协调EEG多尺度表示，并采用轴向时空注意力，以仅5.0M参数在多数BCI基准上取得最高平均平衡准确率。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pre-training
匹配 模型架构：attention mechanism

papers.title: Mitigating Agentic Deception via Evaluation-Side Partially Observable Games
papers.abstract_en: As large language models become more capable agents, they can exhibit deceptive behaviors, cheating human for higher rewards while appearing helpful. We attribute this failure to evaluation-side partial observability, where models are evaluated mainly from final outcome, without checking the faithfulness of underlying reasoning, tool use, and environmental effects. Prior mitigations address this partial observability by predefined evaluator latent belief space or one-shot monitoring, which do not extend to free-form language space and vulnerable to stronger deceptions that evade simple monitoring. In this work, we formulate deception mitigation as an Evaluation-Side Partially Observable Extensive Form Game (e-PoG), a max-min framework in which an agent maximizes reward, a monitor minimizes the agent's payoff by exposing deception from the full interaction trajectory, and a fixed verifier validates the monitor's claims and converts them into penalties. We define the solution concept as a Subgame-Perfect Oversight Equilibrium (SPOE) between agent and monitor, and prove its existence in finite games. With a perfect verifier, every SPOE is faithful; with an imperfect verifier, the guarantee persists if verifier errors do not reverse the ranking of monitor actions. To achieve faithful SPOE, we derive a two-timescale policy gradient algorithm and enhance the pipeline empirically with NLI verification and deterministic checks. Experiments with Gemma3-4B-IT and Qwen3-4B/8B on Agentic Role-Playing, SearchQA, and WebShop show that e-PoG mitigates multiple emergent deception modes, outperforming the strongest baselines by 26.0% in deception mitigation and by up to 39.8% in task success. These gains persist under weak-to-strong supervision. Code is available at https://github.com/Toyoid/deceptive-agent.
papers.abstract_zh: 随着大语言模型成为能力更强的智能体，它们可能表现出欺骗行为，为获取更高奖励而欺骗人类，同时表现得乐于助人。我们将这一失败归因于评估侧的部分可观测性，即模型主要根据最终结果被评估，而不检查其底层推理、工具使用和环境影响的忠实性。此前的缓解方法通过预定义的评估器潜在信念空间或一次性监控来应对这种部分可观测性，但这些方法无法扩展到自由形式的语言空间，并且容易受到规避简单监控的更强欺骗行为的攻击。在本工作中，我们将欺骗缓解形式化为评估侧部分可观测扩展式博弈（e-PoG），这是一个最大最小框架，其中智能体最大化奖励，监控器通过从完整交互轨迹中揭露欺骗来最小化智能体的收益，固定的验证器验证监控器的主张并将其转化为惩罚。我们将解概念定义为智能体与监控器之间的子博弈完美监督均衡（SPOE），并证明其在有限博弈中的存在性。在完美验证器下，每个SPOE都是忠实的；在非完美验证器下，如果验证器错误不逆转监控器动作的排序，该保证仍然成立。为实现忠实的SPOE，我们推导了一个双时间尺度策略梯度算法，并通过NLI验证和确定性检查在经验上增强了流程。在Agentic Role-Playing、SearchQA和WebShop上使用Gemma3-4B-IT和Qwen3-4B/8B进行的实验表明，e-PoG缓解了多种涌现的欺骗模式，在欺骗缓解方面比最强基线高出26.0%，在任务成功率上高出最多39.8%。这些增益在弱到强监督下仍然保持。代码可在https://github.com/Toyoid/deceptive-agent获取。
papers.tldr_zh: 将欺骗缓解建模为评估侧部分可观测扩展式博弈（e-PoG），以监控器揭露欺骗、验证器施加惩罚，并用双时间尺度策略梯度求解子博弈完美监督均衡，在多个任务上同时提升欺骗缓解与任务成功率。

evidence: 开放资源信号：code is available

papers.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
papers.abstract_en: Foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora develop emergent capabilities, tasks that go beyond the training objective. We extend this paradigm to multimodal biology with Bonbon, a foundation model for molecular interactions trained on approximately 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences. From a single representation space, Bonbon exhibits three zero-shot emergent capabilities at hierarchical levels of resolution: functional (mechanism of action), residue (binding site localization, including orthosteric/allosteric discrimination), and bond (covalent versus non-covalent engagement). All three capabilities generalize to out-of-distribution complexes. Bonbon was trained on protein-ligand sequences alone, without any task-specific supervision and without structural coordinates. We conducted controlled scaling experiments across six model scales from 42M to 1.6B parameters; every capability evaluated shows a sharp jump at the largest scale on continuous metrics, even as pretraining loss decreases smoothly. This demonstrates that loss-based scaling laws alone are insufficient to predict when zero-shot emergent capabilities become available. The capabilities reported here emerge after training at a 1:2,000 parameter-to-token ratio to accommodate the sparsity of paired biological interaction data. The same frozen representations achieve state-of-the-art binding and affinity prediction at five orders of magnitude greater speed than co-folding methods. In prospective wet-lab validation across nine disease targets spanning seven protein families, Bonbon achieves a 61.5% dose-response hit rate on de novo compounds, yielding structurally novel molecules not previously reported to inhibit these proteins, including for out-of-distribution targets.
papers.abstract_zh: 在大规模无标签语料上训练的基础模型会发展出涌现能力，即超越训练目标的任务。我们将这一范式扩展到多模态生物学，提出Bonbon，一个在约3.2万亿token的配对蛋白质-配体序列上训练的分子相互作用基础模型。从单一表示空间出发，Bonbon在分层分辨率上展现三种零样本涌现能力：功能（作用机制）、残基（结合位点定位，包括正构/变构区分）和键（共价与非共价结合）。这三种能力均能泛化到分布外复合物。Bonbon仅基于蛋白质-配体序列训练，没有任何任务特定监督，也没有结构坐标。我们在从42M到1.6B参数的六个模型规模上进行受控缩放实验；在连续指标上，所评估的每种能力均在最大规模处出现急剧跃升，即使预训练损失平滑下降。这表明仅凭基于损失的缩放定律不足以预测零样本涌现能力何时可用。此处报告的能力在1:2,000的参数与token比例下训练后涌现，以适应配对生物相互作用数据的稀疏性。相同的冻结表示在比共折叠方法快五个数量级的速度下实现最先进的结合和亲和力预测。在涵盖七个蛋白质家族的九个疾病靶点的前瞻性湿实验验证中，Bonbon在从头化合物上达到61.5%的剂量反应命中率，产生结构新颖的分子，这些分子此前未被报道能抑制这些蛋白质，包括对分布外靶点。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出Bonbon分子相互作用基础模型，仅用蛋白质-配体序列训练即零样本涌现功能、残基和键层面的能力，并在湿实验中取得61.5%剂量反应命中率。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pretraining
偏好加分 scaling-and-compute：scaling law, scaling laws

papers.title: MoSTE: Mixture of Spatio-Temporal Experts for Deepfake Detection in Videos
papers.abstract_en: Generalizable deepfake video detection remains challenging because forgery artifacts vary substantially across manipulation types and often combine diverse spatial and temporal inconsistencies. Existing parameter-efficient adaptation methods typically rely on a single shared representation, rendering them prone to manipulation-specific bias and limiting transfer to unseen forgeries. To address this challenge, we propose Mixture Of Spatio-Temporal Experts (MoSTE), an adaptation framework that enables conditional specialization of forensic representations. Instead of forcing one adapter to model all forgery patterns, MoSTE decomposes adaptation into parallel spatial and temporal expert pools and dynamically routes tokens to the most relevant experts through an unsupervised token-level routing mechanism. This allows experts to naturally specialize in complementary forgery cues without requiring explicit manipulation labels or multi-stage training, while effectively transferring representations from CLIP to the video domain. Extensive experiments across cross-dataset and cross-manipulation benchmarks demonstrate that MoSTE sets a new state of the art in average generalization while preserving strong performance across diverse manipulation families. Additional analysis of expert routing and attention behavior reveals the emergence of expert diversity, suggesting that MoSTE learns complementary spatio-temporal forensic features. Code is available at https://github.com/charbelyah/MoSTE
papers.abstract_zh: 可泛化的深度伪造视频检测仍具挑战性，因为伪造痕迹在不同操纵类型间差异显著，且常混合多样的空间与时间不一致性。现有参数高效适配方法通常依赖单一共享表示，使其易受特定操纵偏差影响，并限制了对未见伪造的迁移能力。为应对这一挑战，我们提出时空专家混合（MoSTE），一种实现取证表示条件化专门化的适配框架。MoSTE不强制单个适配器建模所有伪造模式，而是将适配分解为并行的空间与时间专家池，并通过无监督的令牌级路由机制将令牌动态路由到最相关的专家。这使专家无需显式操纵标签或多阶段训练即可自然专门化于互补的伪造线索，同时有效地将表示从CLIP迁移到视频领域。跨数据集和跨操纵基准的大量实验表明，MoSTE在平均泛化性上树立了新的最先进水平，同时在多种操纵类别上保持强劲性能。对专家路由和注意力行为的额外分析揭示了专家多样性的涌现，表明MoSTE学到了互补的时空取证特征。代码见https://github.com/charbelyah/MoSTE。
papers.tldr_zh: 该文提出时空专家混合框架MoSTE，将CLIP适配分解为并行的空间与时间专家池，用无监督令牌级路由动态选择专家，无需操纵标签或多阶段训练，在跨数据集与跨操纵基准上取得新的平均泛化最先进水平，并观察到专家多样性的涌现。

开放资源信号：code is available

papers.title: Reframe: Observation-Aligned Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Visual Reasoning
papers.abstract_en: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) offer complementary routes to post-training. For visual agents, however, tool use presents two related challenges. Models may overlook useful tool-returned observations, while poorly grounded actions can limit the evidence available for subsequent distillation. We introduce Reframe, a post-training framework that treats the observation state, rather than only the output distribution, as an object of alignment. First, Ground-Drop-GRPO (GD-GRPO) trains spatial and temporal specialists with evidence-aware rewards and stochastic removal of the original visual input, encouraging them to acquire grounded evidence and use the returned observations. Second, Observation-Gated-MOPD (OG-MOPD) replaces deficient tool actions with canonical ones mid-rollout and resumes distillation from the repaired observation. The two stages complement each other, as learning to rely on tool-returned observations can help the policy benefit from observation repair. Neither stage requires a task-specific SFT cold start. Extensive experiments over 14 image and video benchmarks demonstrate that Reframe outperforms both Mix-RL and vanilla MOPD. Ablation results show that GD-GRPO increases observation dependence and tool gain compared with outcome-based GRPO.
papers.abstract_zh: 智能体强化学习（RL）和多教师在线策略蒸馏（MOPD）为后训练提供了互补的途径。然而，对于视觉智能体，工具使用带来了两个相关的挑战。模型可能忽视有用的工具返回观测，而基础不牢的动作可能限制后续蒸馏可用的证据。我们引入Reframe，一个后训练框架，它将观测状态而不仅仅是输出分布视为对齐对象。首先，Ground-Drop-GRPO（GD-GRPO）使用证据感知奖励和原始视觉输入的随机移除来训练空间和时间专家，鼓励它们获取有根据的证据并使用返回的观测。其次，Observation-Gated-MOPD（OG-MOPD）在rollout中途用规范动作替换有缺陷的工具动作，并从修复后的观测恢复蒸馏。这两个阶段相辅相成，因为学习依赖工具返回的观测可以帮助策略从观测修复中受益。两个阶段都不需要任务特定的SFT冷启动。在14个图像和视频基准上的大量实验表明，Reframe优于Mix-RL和原始MOPD。消融结果表明，与基于结果的GRPO相比，GD-GRPO增加了观测依赖性和工具增益。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出Reframe后训练框架，以观测状态为对齐对象：先用GD-GRPO训练专家依赖工具返回观测，再用OG-MOPD在rollout中修复工具动作并恢复蒸馏，在14个图像与视频基准上优于Mix-RL和原始MOPD。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：post-training
evidence: 实验或理论证据信号：ablation, extensive experiment

papers.title: Looking One Step Ahead: An Anticipation-guided Agent for Object State Readout in Videos
papers.abstract_en: Understanding the progress of an activity requires tracking how the objects involved change over time. Object state readout provides this information by describing a target object's states and transitions across video frames. Although multimodal large language models (MLLMs) generate detailed visual descriptions, these descriptions may leave the attributes needed to distinguish successive states insufficiently specified. In this paper, we propose look-ahead state readout (LASER), an anticipation-guided agent for object state readout that uses possible next-step changes to determine which attributes to inspect in the present. Given temporally ordered frames and a target object, LASER converts anticipated changes into targeted visual questions and inspects the current frame to establish attribute values. It then checks state readouts and forecasts against independent observations of subsequent frames, refining a state record used to generate the final description. Reusable textual observation skills guide this process and are refined by tracing discrepancies with reference captions to the responsible instructions. Candidate revisions are selected on separate videos based on improved caption quality without increased contradictions with reference facts. Model parameters remain frozen throughout adaptation and inference, and the revised skills remain fixed during evaluation. Experiment results and further analysis on OSCaR and PLM RCap show consistent improvements of LASER over strong baselines and existing approaches, which demonstrates the effectiveness of our approach.
papers.abstract_zh: 理解活动的进展需要跟踪所涉及物体如何随时间变化。物体状态读出通过描述目标物体在视频帧中的状态和转换来提供这一信息。尽管多模态大语言模型（MLLM）能生成详细的视觉描述，但这些描述可能未能充分指定区分连续状态所需的属性。在本文中，我们提出前瞻状态读出（LASER），一种用于物体状态读出的预期引导智能体，它使用可能的下一步变化来确定当前应检查哪些属性。给定按时间排序的帧和目标物体，LASER将预期的变化转化为有针对性的视觉问题，并检查当前帧以确定属性值。然后，它根据对后续帧的独立观测来检查状态读出和预测，精炼用于生成最终描述的状态记录。可复用的文本观测技能指导这一过程，并通过将差异追溯到参考字幕来精炼这些技能。候选修订在单独视频上根据字幕质量提升且不增加与参考事实的矛盾来选择。模型参数在适应和推理过程中保持冻结，修订后的技能在评估期间保持固定。在OSCaR和PLM RCap上的实验结果和进一步分析表明，LASER相比强基线和现有方法取得了一致改进，证明了我们方法的有效性。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出预期引导的智能体LASER，将可能的下一步变化转化为针对性视觉问题以读出当前物体状态，并用后续帧独立观测校验与精炼状态记录，在OSCaR和PLM RCap上一致优于强基线。

匹配 MLLM / VLM：multimodal large language model

papers.title: Obscured Wildfire Flame Detection by Spatio-temporal Analysis of Smoke Patterns Using Frame-wise Transformers
papers.abstract_en: In this paper, we propose a new paradigm in wildfire management for detecting both visible and obscured fire using Deep Learning (DL). The essence of our method is the joint spatial and temporal analysis of RGB videos, embracing the fact that temporal patterns of smoke motions in consecutive video frames can indicate obscured fire flames. This perspective contrasts the traditional approach of independently analyzing images and individual video frames. To this end, we propose a frame-wise transformer architecture that applies an attention mechanism between the consecutive frames while preserving spatial information within frames as opposed to regular attention mechanisms like the non-local block, which combines spatial and temporal information into a single vector. We also optimize the temporal pattern lengths under different spatial resolutions to achieve the highest performance while reducing the computational cost. To investigate the applicability of our method in aerial image processing, we applied it to a curated version of the FLAME2 dataset that includes dual-mode RGB/IR videos. The IR video feed is used to extract ground truth, while the model is trained only on RGB videos to maintain applicability to lowcost commercial drones (which are equipped only with regular cameras) and facilitate processing existing RGB-only datasets. Our proposed method achieves a Segmentation Foreground Dice score of 92.61%, an Object Detection Precision and Recall rate of 93.21% and 91.73%, and clip-level classification accuracy of 98.02%, respectively. We also investigated the efficacy and generalizability of our method through ablation study
papers.abstract_zh: 本文提出一种野火管理的新范式，利用深度学习（DL）检测可见火焰与被遮挡火焰。该方法的核心是对RGB视频进行联合的时空分析，利用连续视频帧中烟雾运动的时间模式可指示被遮挡火焰这一事实。这一视角与独立分析图像和单个视频帧的传统方法形成对比。为此，我们提出一种逐帧Transformer架构，在连续帧之间应用注意力机制，同时保留帧内空间信息，这与非局部块等将时空信息合并为单一向量的常规注意力机制不同。我们还在不同空间分辨率下优化时间模式长度，以在降低计算成本的同时实现最高性能。为探究该方法在航拍图像处理中的适用性，我们将其应用于经过整理的FLAME2数据集，该数据集包含双模态RGB/IR视频。IR视频流用于提取真值，而模型仅在RGB视频上训练，以保持对低成本商用无人机（仅配备普通相机）的适用性，并便于处理仅含RGB的现有数据集。所提方法分别达到92.61%的分割前景Dice分数、93.21%和91.73%的目标检测精确率与召回率，以及98.02%的片段级分类准确率。我们还通过消融研究考察了该方法的有效性与泛化性。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出逐帧Transformer对RGB视频中烟雾的时空模式进行联合分析，以检测可见与被遮挡的野火火焰，在FLAME2数据集上取得92.61%分割Dice与98.02%片段级分类准确率。
why_it_matters: 匹配 模型架构：transformer architecture, attention mechanism
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: ProofCoder: Continuous Reasoning for Automated Software Verification
papers.abstract_en: Formal verification using proof assistants provides strong correctness guarantees for software, but constructing proofs remains labor-intensive and requires significant expertise. Recent approaches based on large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in automating proof synthesis. However, these approaches typically constrain the model to a rigid tactic-generation loop, in which the surrounding system controls premise retrieval, proof-state management, and backtracking. We introduce ProofCoder, an agentic proof-synthesis system for Rocq that approaches theorem proving from a coding-agent perspective. Rather than generating tactics within a fixed loop, ProofCoder reasons continuously throughout proof search and uses proof-assistant feedback to decide when to gather additional information, inspect proof states, revise previously generated proof fragments, or backtrack to an earlier point in the proof. This allows it to iteratively construct, repair, and refine proofs, at either tactic-level or whole-proof granularity. We evaluate ProofCoder on 280 challenging verification tasks from the AutoRocq Benchmark. On the best-performing configurations, ProofCoder increases proof success from 47% to 60% over the state-of-theart AutoRocq system, corresponding to a 27.7% relative improvement at approximately half the cost. Our ablations identify continuous reasoning as a key design choice: without it, the agent solves fewer lemmas at substantially higher cost, backtracks four to six times more often, and more frequently discards its own revisions. Whole-proof and tactic-level generation achieve similar success rates but follow distinct search and repair strategies. These results suggest that effective automated software verification requires more than improved tactic selection: continuous reasoning and feedback-guided proof revision are critical ingredients for robust proof synthesis.
papers.abstract_zh: 使用证明助手的形式化验证为软件提供了强正确性保证，但构造证明仍然劳动密集且需要大量专业知识。基于大语言模型（LLM）的近期方法在自动化证明合成方面显示出前景。然而，这些方法通常将模型限制在僵化的策略生成循环中，由周围系统控制前提检索、证明状态管理和回溯。我们引入ProofCoder，一个面向Rocq的智能体式证明合成系统，从编码智能体的视角处理定理证明。ProofCoder不在固定循环内生成策略，而是在整个证明搜索过程中持续推理，并利用证明助手反馈来决定何时收集额外信息、检查证明状态、修订先前生成的证明片段或回溯到证明中的较早位置。这使其能够在策略级或整体证明粒度上迭代构造、修复和精炼证明。我们在AutoRocq基准的280个挑战性验证任务上评估ProofCoder。在表现最佳的配置上，ProofCoder将证明成功率从47%提升至60%，相比最先进的AutoRocq系统，在约一半成本下实现27.7%的相对提升。我们的消融实验确定持续推理是关键设计选择：没有它，智能体解决的引理更少且成本显著更高，回溯频率高四到六倍，并更频繁地丢弃自己的修订。整体证明和策略级生成达到相似的成功率，但遵循不同的搜索和修复策略。这些结果表明，有效的自动化软件验证需要的不仅仅是改进的策略选择：持续推理和反馈引导的证明修订是稳健证明合成的关键要素。

papers.title: MNN-Pocket-0.3B Technical Report
papers.abstract_en: This technical report presents MNN-Pocket-0.3B, a compact 300M-parameter dense language model designed for efficient on-device deployment and supporting context lengths of up to 32K tokens. With an INT4 deployment footprint of only 173 MB and decoding throughput of up to 466 tokens/s on iPad Pro M5 (Metal), it can be seamlessly integrated into applications on edge devices such as smartphones and smart glasses. MNN-Pocket-0.3B is developed through the co-design of its architecture, data, training pipeline, and inference system. Hardware-aware architecture selection and dependency-aware vocabulary pruning balance model capability with on-device memory and compute constraints. A four-stage pre-training pipeline covering approximately 4.1 trillion high-quality Chinese and English tokens equips the model with broad knowledge and reasoning capabilities. This is followed by a three-stage post-training pipeline comprising instruction fine-tuning, multi-teacher on-policy distillation, and quantization-aware training. Finally, hardware-specific optimizations in the MNN inference engine enable fast, memory-efficient inference and long-context processing. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that MNN-Pocket-0.3B achieves frontier-level performance among models of comparable size, with particularly strong results in Chinese and English knowledge and reasoning, mathematics, coding, and instruction following. It consistently outperforms similarly sized open-source models and even surpasses several 0.5B-parameter models on instruction-following benchmarks. We release MNN-Pocket-0.3B with open weights and ready-to-use MNN deployment packages. We hope it will provide a practical foundation for capable, responsive, and memory-efficient edge applications while advancing research and development in on-device language models.

papers.title: KiteNorm: Variance Regularisation for Stable and Scalable Post-LN Transformers
papers.abstract_en: Post-LayerNorm Transformers have seen limited practical adoption due to enduring difficulties in scaling them to large depths. While prior research has focused on stabilising Post-LayerNorm by improving conditioning at initialisation, stability often deteriorates when models are trained with large learning rates, forcing additional compromises. In the decoder-only settings we study, existing Post-LayerNorm methods fail to outperform strong Pre-LayerNorm baselines. We propose KiteNorm, a post-norm training method designed to break this trend by constraining hidden-state variance. This approach is motivated by a bound on the LayerNorm Jacobian suggesting that variance growth contributes to gradient vanishing, alongside empirical evidence linking it to rank collapse. KiteNorm combines residual scaling and variance regularisation to maintain stability throughout training, supported by scalarised double-normalisation that provides separately learnable scales for the skip and residual branches. Across decoder-only Transformers up to 1.3B parameters, KiteNorm improves training stability and outperforms leading baselines at their optimal learning rates, with scaling laws favouring KiteNorm across depth, width, batch size, and training budget. Ablations show that each component is necessary for the full stability and performance gains.

papers.title: EVAThink: Evidence Sufficiency-Guided Training for Adaptive Thinking in Video Understanding
papers.abstract_en: Under a fixed frame budget, video understanding with vision-language models (VLMs) depends on whether the sampled frames provide sufficient evidence for the question. Sufficient frame evidence supports direct answering, whereas less informative observations may benefit from reasoning that connects the available cues. We introduce EVAThink, which enhances video understanding through evidence sufficiency-guided training for adaptive thinking. First, Recoverable Evidence Gap Mining constructs evidence-dense and evidence-sparse video views that share the same question and answer under an identical frame budget. It retains pairs where sparse views yield lower direct-answer accuracy than dense views but benefit from explicit reasoning, providing supervision for response-mode selection. Second, Evidence-Guided Two-Stage Reinforcement Learning uses stage-specific rewards to guide training with evidence-based mode preferences and then refine response efficiency, while first-token advantage regularization mitigates mode collapse. Trained on only 6.7K curated samples, EVAThink consistently improves upon the base model across video understanding benchmarks under both 32- and 64-frame budgets, while outperforming strong baselines on average. The code, model, and datasets are available at \href{https://github.com/ChangtiWu/EVAThink}{EVAThink}.

papers.title: OnlyAct: Extracting Action Representations from Foundation Models for World Models
papers.abstract_en: Video world models promise general-purpose interactive simulators, but their training is limited by action supervision: action labels are scarce, fragmented across incompatible specifications, and do not scale with the unlabeled video pretraining corpus. A common workaround jointly trains an action encoder to compress consecutive frames into a latent action and a decoder to reconstruct the next frame from the previous frame and that latent, forcing the latent to capture only new information. This has two limitations: learning the action space from scratch can limit generalization to unseen domains, and the bottleneck trades expressiveness for separation, with tighter settings losing nuance and looser ones risking scene leakage under domain shifts. We argue for a different starting point: rather than learning actions from scratch, we start from a pretrained foundation model (V-JEPA 2), whose embeddings of a frame pair already carry substantial action information after large-scale, diverse video pretraining. The remaining challenge is to extract the action while discarding the scene. We propose a label-free contrastive adaptation framework that pulls together frame pairs sharing the same motion under a different scene and pushes apart pairs from the same scene with different motion, reshaping the geometry of the pretrained space without imposing a reconstruction bottleneck. We introduce a unified evaluation protocol along three axes (action expressiveness, scene invariance, and action-conditioned video generation quality) across robot manipulation, camera navigation, game, and driving benchmarks, most of which are unseen during adaptation. Compared with annotation-free latent-action methods, our representations are substantially more expressive while matching their scene invariance, and they yield world models that transfer demonstrated actions to new scenes more faithfully.

papers.title: Tree-Ising: Repairing Language Models with Bit-Level Ising Edits
papers.abstract_en: Weight-space programming, introduced in recent MIT work by Takehi et al., enables a frontier LLM agent to read a network's weights and write a repair. Their GPT-6 Astra agent corrected the reasoning loops of Qwen3.5-0.8B without gradients, using 158 agent turns, 89.7 million tokens, and 50 forward-pass requests. Our method, Tree-Ising, casts this repair as a sparse discrete optimization problem over the model's own BF16 weights. Forward statistics define an objective that weakens a loop direction, strengthens a concluding direction, and preserves the layer's output on productive tokens. Within a state-tree representation, where lossless BF16 storage acts as a special case, the admissible edits are sign flips and exponent shifts that preserve all shared group exponents and mantissas. We decompose this objective exactly into independent QUBO (Ising) problems, one per output row, which we solve on a GPU using simulated annealing or quantum-inspired simulated bifurcation. On the agent's two layers, Tree-Ising achieves 54.6% on MATH-500, outperforming the agent's edit (51.7%) under the same evaluation protocol, while the base model scores 7.9% as reported. The simulated bifurcation solver yields a statistically indistinguishable repair at 55.1%. Both solvers outperform the agent edit across all five math benchmarks, with statistically significant improvements on MATH-500 and GSM8K after correcting for multiple comparisons. Our approach modifies 13% to 17% fewer weights and reduces BF16 bit flips by a factor of 2.2 to 2.3. It requires only four forward-pass requests and zero LLM tokens, with the annealing recipe costing about $0.90 in GPU time. On Qwen3.5-2B, with layers and dose selected using only the base model, the same recipe increases greedy GSM8K accuracy from 21.6% to 69.4%. As a proof of concept, we execute an eight-variable repair subproblem using QAOA on an IBM Heron processor.

papers.title: Sable: A Small-Field Sumcheck Argument for Bit-Exact Inference of Large Language Models
papers.abstract_en: We present Sable, an argument system and single-GPU prover for the statement that a committed, integer-quantized transformer produced a given token sequence from a given prompt, bit for bit. Sable fixes an integer function F_O with no floating-point step, in which every rounding, normalization, softmax and sampling decision is determined by its inputs, and proves it with a constraint system whose relations provably never wrap modulo the 31-bit KoalaBear prime. The proof batches zerochecks and LogUp-GKR lookups into one sumcheck per domain, and commits to every witness tensor and weight in one multilinear commitment built from Reed-Solomon codes, BLAKE3 Merkle trees and a mixed-length BaseFold opening. The prover streams the model layer by layer on one GPU. On one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU, Sable proves all 64 layers of Qwen2.5-32B in 92.5 s for 4,096 tokens and 398 s for 16,384 tokens, and covers Qwen3-32B and the mixture-of-experts Qwen3-30B-A3B (4,096 tokens in 121.8 and 84.7 s). A proof costs 41 to 50 times the serving time, or 6.4 cents per 4,096-token request at public GPU prices, and 40 to 64 times less time per parameter and token than zkLLM. On WikiText-2, F_O's greedy token matches the BF16 model's at 86.3% of positions; on Qwen3, F_O is within 1.6 points of BF16 on MMLU and 1.7 points on GSM8K. A verifier with a compiled core checks a proof on one CPU core in 19 to 56 s. In the random-oracle model, the interactive proof has round-by-round soundness error 2^-103. The proof is not zero-knowledge, so the system targets open-weight models. Code: https://github.com/moonmath-ai/Sable

papers.title: Cognitive Multi-Agent Search and Rescue: Language-Grounded Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Collaborative Robotics
papers.abstract_en: Effective search and rescue (SAR) operations require autonomous systems capable of coordinating multiple heterogeneous agents, adapting to dynamic hazards, and aligning with human mission intent. Existing language-guided reinforcement learning (RL) methods primarily focus on single-agent instruction following and lack mechanisms for team-level coordination in complex, partially observable environments. This paper presents a Cognitive Multi-Agent Framework based on Language-Grounded Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (LG-HRL) that integrates natural-language understanding, hierarchical policy decomposition, and a shared cognitive workspace to achieve cohesive multi-agent behavior in SAR scenarios. Human instructions are interpreted by a large language model (LLM) and transformed into structured semantic cues that guide high-level strategy selection and role assignment across UAV and UGV agents. A formal Language-Grounded Multi-Agent Hierarchical Decision Process (LG-MAHDP) is introduced to model the interplay between semantic grounding, hierarchical control, and distributed coordination. Comprehensive experiments in a simulated disaster environment show that LG-HRL improves learning speed by 2.3 times, increases coordination coherence by 37%, and enhances subgoal accuracy and hazard avoidance by 46% and 31%, respectively. The system achieves 20-30% higher victim rescue rates, demonstrates emergent role specialization, and adapts immediately to human verbal updates. Ablation studies confirm that both the shared cognitive workspace and language grounding are critical to overall system performance. Overall, this work establishes a new paradigm for language-guided multi-agent SAR robotics, demonstrating that semantic grounding combined with hierarchical reasoning enables safer, more efficient, and more interpretable autonomous rescue operations.

papers.title: Ceci n'est pas une pipe -- Toward a Symbolic Solver for the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus Using Evolutionary Computation
papers.abstract_en: The Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC) is a benchmark designed to assess the capability of Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems to generalize starting from a few samples, a task humans excel at. The ARC-AGI contests held since 2020 have been the focus of intense competition, with participants proposing approaches ranging from traditional symbolic AI to Transformer architectures. Despite a long history of successes, evolutionary algorithms (EAs) were notably absent from the approaches appearing in the main contest. As score-and-search program synthesis approaches, EAs suffer from issues related to choosing the proper representation in the Domain-Specific Language applied to the problem (for example, pixel-level or object-level), and distinguishing between two candidate solutions producing the same outputs. In this work, we present the first fully symbolic, evolutionary-based program synthesis approach submitted to the ARC-AGI-2 main contest. The main contributions are: evolving the grid parser and the output projector together with the program that transforms the grid, so that a task-specific language emerges during program synthesis; grounding the symbols the parser can extract in core knowledge theory from cognitive psychology; and an object-aware fitness that grades partially correct outputs beyond pixel-level discrepancies.

papers.title: A computational framework for understanding embodied plans
papers.abstract_en: Reasoning about people's plans and goals based on their actions is fundamental to human social interaction and essential for cooperative, embodied artificial intelligence. Formalizing this capacity in naturalistic, embodied settings has been a longstanding challenge. Here, we present GenEA, a novel agent representation capable of reasoning over multi-step, long-horizon embodied plans. At the heart of GenEA lies a multilevel state-space that couples the coarse biomechanics of an articulated body and its interactions with nearby objects by extending the task-and-motion planning framework from robotics with simulation-based intuitive physics. By embedding this state-space in a generative model, GenEA yields a joint probability distribution over goals and embodied plans. Across several experiments spanning the qualitatively distinct domains of object manipulation and navigation, featuring diverse tasks and multiple behavioral measures, we show that GenEA, through simple transformations of this joint distribution, recapitulates how humans reason about embodied plans. Crucially, GenEA consistently outperforms strong alternative models, including plausible heuristics, standard task-and-motion planning, and a state-of-the-art vision-language model. GenEA thereby offers a new perspective on the architecture of human reasoning and social cognition, suggesting that embodied artificial intelligence systems seeking to seamlessly interact with humans should adopt GenEA-like generative models of action planning.

papers.title: CASCADE: Constraint-Aware SCAffolded DEcomposition for Logical Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract_en: Logical Anomaly Detection (LAD) requires verifying whether all category-specific constraints, such as object counts, pairing relations, and measurement ranges, are satisfied by a query image given only a few normal references. Recent LAD methods based on Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) formulate this as checklist verification, decomposing the decision into independent textual checks. This decomposition, however, is text-only. Every item still reads the same unmodified query image, so the LVLM must extract different forms of visual evidence from one raw image. We identify this text-image mismatch as a constraint-specific perception gap, the source of two failure modes: instance conflation for binding constraints and scale drift for calibration constraints. To diagnose whether these failures stem from insufficient reasoning or insufficient perception, we compare textual reasoning guides and visual perception guides in a training-free setting. Our analysis shows that reasoning over the same image provides little benefit, whereas adapting the visual input to each constraint substantially improves verification accuracy. Based on this finding, we propose CASCADE, a training-free framework that extends checklist decomposition using constraint-specific visual scaffolds. We further introduce CASCADE++, which adapts these scaffolds at the object level by deriving their configurations from the constraint structure and reference distribution. Across MVTec-LOCO and VID-AD, CASCADE++ surpasses the full-shot state of the art by 3.9 AUROC points with only three references, and improves over the strongest VID-AD baseline by 11.4, transferring across multiple LVLM backbones without any training.

papers.title: OptiCover: A Scalable and Multi-Surface Framework for Cold-Start Visual Optimization under Semantic Constraints
papers.abstract_en: Selecting an effective cover photo is a critical yet understudied problem in visual merchandising for e-commerce marketplaces. On Airbnb, hosts upload many photos depicting different rooms, amenities, and points of interest, but must manually choose a single static cover photo that is reused across heterogeneous product surfaces. This creates substantial challenges: over 90\% of listing photos have no engagement labels, leading to a severe cold-start regime; guest preferences vary across surfaces and search intents, and visually captivating photos may be semantically misaligned with the underlying listing. At Airbnb scale, this corresponds to hundreds of millions of photos and hundreds of thousands of new uploads per day. We propose \emph{OptiCover}, a scalable framework for cold-start visual optimization under semantic constraints and multi-surface engagement signals. The framework combines (i) a photo candidate generator that identifies candidate photos through various proxies, (ii) lightweight vision heads applied to frozen CLIP embeddings for large-scale semantic scoring, (iii) a cross-modal grounding validator based on a vision-language model (VLM) that enforces semantic representativeness, and (iv) an Exploration Logging Module (ELM) that orchestrates the collection of randomized engagement data across heterogeneous product surfaces and contextual search intents. We evaluate OptiCover through extensive offline studies and multiple online experiments across HomePage, and Search surfaces. OptiCover is now deployed in production and performs tens of millions of photo swaps daily. Online results show a 1.5\% engagement lift on the HomePage and a 0.35\% increase in bookers on Search, generating millions of dollars in incremental revenue. Our findings suggest that action-space shaping and semantic constraints are primary drivers of performance.

papers.title: Deterministic, Reproducible Inference in Exact Integer Arithmetic, and Verifiable Distributed Inference as Its Consequence
papers.abstract_en: Optimized floating-point inference is not reproducible across environments: the same model on different hardware, compilers or thread counts can produce different bits. We present tritify, an open-source runtime that executes the forward pass of real models -- decoder-only language models, Mixture-of-Experts decoders, and the Segment Anything 2.1 image/video stack -- with the entire run-time path in exact integer arithmetic; floating point is confined to offline quantization and the float reference used for verification. We make three separate claims and verify each. (1) Cross-hardware reproducibility: the integer path produces bit-identical output run to run, across CPU instruction-set architectures, and across CPU/GPU, carried by a reproducing SHA-256 of the output. (2) Decision fidelity: the integer path reproduces the float reference's decision on the models and inputs tested, with the numeric exceptions measured; per-layer fidelity through sixteen layers of OLMoE-1B-7B and of a 106-billion-parameter MoE shows no fidelity cliff. (3) Location independence: a model's computation can be split across instruction sets, CPU and GPU, and networked machines with zero effect on the output bits. GLM-4.5-Air (106,852,251,264 parameters, 427 GB of integer codes) generated its answer across three machines, none of which can hold its integer codes in RAM, bit-identically to a single-host reference. The consequence is verifiable distributed inference: an untrusted server or a fleet of devices runs the model while an open scalar oracle re-derives the exact bytes; a guarantee against a dishonest server is future work. We do not claim a per-device speed-up, bit-equality of floating-valued intermediates, or confidentiality. Code: https://github.com/pelloran-inc/tritify

papers.title: MOAI: Module-Optimizing Architecture for non-interactive secure transformer Inference
papers.abstract_en: Privacy concerns have been raised in Large Language Models (LLM) inference when models are deployed in Cloud Service Providers (CSP). Homomorphic encryption (HE) offers a promising solution by enabling secure inference directly over encrypted inputs. However, the high computational overhead of HE remains a major bottleneck. To address this challenge, we propose MOAI, an efficient HE-based, non-interactive framework for secure transformer inference. MOAI gains significant efficiency improvement from: (1) a novel evaluation flow that combines column and diagonal packing with consistent strategies across all layers, eliminating expensive format conversions. (2) rotation-free algorithms for Softmax and LayerNorm that significantly reduce the number of costly HE rotations, removing 2,448 HE rotations in BERT-base inference. (3) Column packing removes rotations in plaintext-ciphertext matrix multiplications and interleaved batching further reduces the rotations in ciphertext-ciphertext matrix multiplications. MOAI uses at least 1.7x fewer HE rotations compared to the state-of-the-art works across all matrix multiplications of BERT-base. As a result, we achieve a $52.8 \%$ reduction in evaluation time compared to the state-of-the-art HE-based non-interactive secure transformer inference, THOR (Moon et al., CCS 25). We then apply MOAI on the Powerformer's framework and achieve a $55.7 \%$ reduction in evaluation time compared to Powerformer (Park et al., ACL 25), which approximates Softmax and LayerNorm with simpler functions in transformer and proposes HE-based non-interactive transformer inference. We report an amortized time of 2.36 minutes per input on a single GPU environment. We show the extendibility by applying MOAI in LLaMA-3-8B. Our implementation is publicly available as open source.

papers.title: How Post-Training Influences Verbalized Algorithmic Computation in Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Post-training improves language-model reasoning, but how it changes the use of internal information and verbalized chain of thought (CoT) remains unclear. We study successive SFT, DPO, and RLVR checkpoints of Olmo-3-7B-Instruct on multi-digit addition, using carry values as known intermediate state. Probes recover carry information from internal activations with similar accuracy in SFT and RLVR, although manipulating this information does not reliably control model outputs. In contrast, the usefulness of verbalized reasoning differs: CoTs produced by RLVR yield higher accuracy across receiving checkpoints than those produced by SFT or DPO. We also show that carry-related statements receive higher importance scores after RLVR than matched random controls. DPO shows similar sensitivity to carry-related statements but without comparable accuracy gains. These results suggest that post-training changes the usefulness of written reasoning and sensitivity to its content in meaningful ways, although greater sensitivity does not necessarily coincide with better problem performance.

papers.title: Prune, Don't Merge: Expert Compression of Mixture-of-Experts LLMs on Multilingual Production Tasks
papers.abstract_en: Mixture-of-Experts language models are cheap to run per token but expensive to hold in GPU memory, which drives the cost of serving them in production. One-shot expert compression shrinks them after a single calibration pass. Its two current state-of-the-art methods are REAP for expert pruning, which deletes the least salient experts, and REAM for expert merging, which merges them into the most salient ones. Both have been evaluated only on academic benchmarks. We compare the two on five multilingual production tasks of a web-hosting company, from classification to the generation of marketing HTML email templates, with two 30B-parameter models (Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 and the hybrid Mamba-attention Nemotron-3.5-Lightning) at 25% and 50% of experts removed and the same calibration data. Pruning wins: on the same rows, REAP is significantly better in 16 of 20 comparisons and REAM in 2. At 25%, REAP keeps 93.6% of Qwen3-30B's generative quality and REAM 62.5%, although on benchmarks the two are within a point for the same model. The damage concentrates in the output contract rather than the content: 89.8-95.2% of each significant loss on email templates comes from hard-gate failures such as invalid JSON, broken mobile layouts and runaway generation, and most failed non-English domain descriptions copy the prompt's English opening phrase. Cross-perplexity and logit divergence, two diagnostics from the REAP paper, also track production quality, as does the rate of repetition loops; n-gram diversity does not. We close with practical guidance for compressing MoE models for production.

papers.title: A Geometric Invariant of Attention Predicts Head Specialization from Weights Alone
papers.abstract_en: Transformers are built with continuous symmetries in the attention mechanism. We derive $ρ$, a scalar invariant that measures each head's capacity to couple to rotary positional encodings. This framework allows us to analyze heads without forward passes, opening a new research direction into data-independent analysis of modern LLMs. Empirically, we find that $ρ$ predicts induction heads, the most-studied circuit type in mechanistic interpretability, with Spearman correlation between $-0.55$ and $-0.74$ across four bias-free RoPE models spanning $135$M to $7$B parameters. As a preliminary proof of concept, we use $ρ$ to apply YaRN to only the top-50% positional heads, which degrades perplexity less than uniform application. Code is available at https://github.com/MPedraBento/rho-invariant.

papers.title: ASPIRE: An Agentic System-Identification Platform for Iterative Reasoning and Exploration
papers.abstract_en: System identification requires expert decisions on the identification method, incorporation of prior physical knowledge, and model validation. We propose ASPIRE, a framework for nonlinear system identification in which a large language model agent selects and executes the identification method. ASPIRE constructs closed-form, nonlinear static or dynamic models from measured data, optionally supplemented by a system description, the intended use of the model, and physical requirements expressed formally or in natural language. Each model includes its parameters, an estimation record, an interpretation of its terms, and an error evaluated on test data inaccessible to the agent. Formal physical requirements are verified independently. ASPIRE operates autonomously or interactively, allowing the agent to ask questions and the user to request further analyses and identification rounds. We evaluate ASPIRE on three measured systems: a mobile robot, a rotational system with dry friction, and a laboratory fermenter. Each system is tested with and without a description, in five runs per task. All 30 runs delivered valid models, at a cost of 0.96 to 3.38 US dollars per run. An assessment by the authors found that, for the 30 models recommended by the agent, one per run, the interpretation of the model and the documentation of its structure selection and parameter estimation fully satisfied 132 of 150 assessed items and partly satisfied 18. The most frequent discrepancy, found in nine models, concerned inaccurate or unsupported claims about model structure selection.

papers.title: Beyond Sunny Skies: Using Large Language Models to Predict Urban Traffic in Adverse Weather
papers.abstract_en: Urban traffic flow prediction is a cornerstone of intelligent transportation systems, yet accurate forecasting under adverse weather conditions remains a significant challenge. Existing data-driven models, while effective for routine patterns, often struggle with the sparse data and complex non-linear shifts associated with rare meteorological events. These methods typically treat environmental contexts as shallow numerical features, failing to capture the underlying semantic reasoning-why and how specific adverse conditions alter mobility behaviors across regions with different functional compositions. To address this limitation, we propose Multi-STG, a unified framework that integrates Large Language Model (LLM)-derived semantic priors with graph-based spatiotemporal learning. Multi-STG introduces an LLM-empowered semantic enhancement module that transforms comprehensive context descriptions such as weather, POIs, and holidays into high-level semantic embeddings, effectively providing a knowledge-driven complement to data scarcity. Furthermore, we design a multimodal attentional fusion mechanism to dynamically weigh heterogeneous inputs and a semantic-enhanced prediction head with gated residual calibration to robustly adjust forecasts based on semantic guidance. Extensive experiments on real-world multi-city private car datasets demonstrate that Multi-STG outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, reducing MAE by 11.82\% on average relative to the strongest baseline across three cities, while maintaining stable performance under sparse and non-stationary conditions.

papers.title: Learning Evidence-Grounded Reasoning for Context-Aware Time Series Forecasting
papers.abstract_en: LLM-driven time series forecasting has become increasingly promising by leveraging contextual features to generate future values directly or refine forecast priors. However, incorporating contextual features alone does not ensure that models can identify which features matter for forecasting and understand what they suggest about future dynamics. We argue that the fundamental challenge is how to extract predictive evidence from contextual features and when and how to leverage it to guide forecasting decisions. In this paper, we propose CastReasoner, an evidence-grounded reasoning model for context-aware time series forecasting. Specifically, CastReasoner uses a structured chain of thought (CoT) to extract predictive evidence from contextual features, infer the future dynamics suggested by this evidence, and assess these dynamics against the forecast prior to guide adaptive forecasting decisions. To enable this capability, we design a reasoning-centric two-stage post-training framework including supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL). First, we synthesize reasoning trajectories through controllable multi-teacher guidance and select high-quality ones using a novel student-aware difficulty metric. Second, we design fine-grained multi-objective rewards to further improve reasoning and forecasting. To address heterogeneous learning needs across domains in both stages, we introduce a convergence-guided data balancing strategy. Through this two-stage training, CastReasoner improves both reasoning quality and predictive accuracy. Extensive experiments across multi-domain forecasting benchmarks demonstrate that CastReasoner achieves superior forecasting performance.

papers.title: ABRR: Transforming Temporal Sentence Grounding with Wasserstein-Adaptive Refinement and Precision Ranking
papers.abstract_en: Temporal Sentence Grounding (TSG) aims to localize temporal segments in untrimmed videos that correspond to natural language queries, a critical task for video understanding with applications in video retrieval, summarization, and human-computer interaction. Despite significant progress driven by transformer-based models, existing TSG methods suffer from two key limitations: quantization errors due to temporal downsampling, which misalign segment boundaries, and suboptimal ranking of predictions based on semantic matching rather than localization precision. To address these challenges, we propose the Adaptive Boundary Refinement and Ranking (ABRR) framework, a novel, model-agnostic post-processing approach that enhances the performance of any TSG model without retraining. ABRR integrates three innovative components: (1) Temporal Distribution Smoothing, which mitigates noise in predicted score distributions using Gaussian kernel convolution; (2) Boundary Refinement via Optimal Transport, which leverages the 2-Wasserstein distance and Sinkhorn iterations to align coarse segment boundaries with true temporal moments, grounded in Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport theory; and (3) Quality-Driven Re-Ranking, which reorders predictions using a composite score balancing localization precision and semantic relevance. By correcting quantization errors and prioritizing accurately localized segments, ABRR achieves substantial improvements over state-of-the-art TSG models. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, including Charades-STA, ActivityNet Captions, and QVHighlights, demonstrate consistent gains at stringent IoU thresholds (e.g., IoU=0.7), alongside enhanced ranking performance. The framework's computational efficiency and compatibility with existing models make it a versatile and impactful solution for real-world TSG applications.

papers.title: Stochastic Projections and Rank-Aware Learning Rates for Federated LoRA
papers.abstract_en: Fine-tuning large-scale foundation models across resource-constrained, distributed clients presents significant computational and communication challenges. While merging Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) with Federated Learning (FL) enables rank-based flexibility, the interdependence of the adaptation matrices ($\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$) often complicates optimization. In this work, we theoretically demonstrate that LoRA fine-tuning with Gaussian initialization and a frozen $\mathbf{A}$ matrix acts as a stochastic approximation of full fine-tuning, where batch gradients are subject to a random, rank-dependent perturbation. Motivated by this insight, we propose freezing and periodically resampling $\mathbf{A}$ matrices at the client level. This strategy decouples the $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ gradients, diminishes LoRA low-rank constraints and reduces both computational and uplink communication overheads by 50\%, allowing for the reallocation of resources toward higher adaptation ranks. Furthermore, we show that in this frozen-$\mathbf{A}$ regime, the adaptation rank $r$ directly governs the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the perturbed gradients. Specifically, we find that the SNR increases linearly with $r$, implying that clients' learning rates must be dynamically scaled with their adaptation ranks for higher utility. Building on these foundations, we introduce SPRA-LoRA (Stochastic Projection Rank-Aware LoRA), a federated rank-aware fine-tuning strategy that utilizes frozen, resampled $\mathbf{A}$ matrices and rank-dependent learning rates for clients. We also prove its convergence with heterogeneous client resources. Our experiments across benchmark datasets demonstrate that SPRA-LoRA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines with half the overhead on clients.

papers.title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract_en: Trained action policies write manipulation skill into network weights, tying what is learned to the distribution it is learned from. In-context learning (ICL) avoids this coupling but has not matched trained policies, because a demonstration recorded in another scene carries no feedback from the world the robot currently faces. We observe that what an agent learns in context is semantic, recording task steps and object roles rather than visual appearance, so experience gathered in one world transfers to another. Based on this insight, we propose World In-Context Learning (WICL), a paradigm in which a frozen model starts from a demonstration, rehearses the task in a world such as a simulator, and writes the feedback into its context rather than its weights. We build RoboScript, a modular infrastructure that implements WICL for agentic manipulation. From a single demonstration, RoboScript learns each task through rehearsal in simulation, freezes the learned knowledge as a Task Memory, and deploys the frozen memory on new scenes with data isolation that ensures every deployment input is available on a real robot. On all 50 tasks of RoboTwin 2.0, RoboScript reaches 83.4% mean success across clean and randomized settings with one demonstration per task and no gradient updates, exceeding the strongest trained action policy by over 20 points. The method generalizes across visual distributions, improves through reflection, scales with the foundation model, and transfers to a physical dual-arm robot through cross-embodiment memory adaptation. With a world in the loop, a robot can learn a manipulation task in its context as well as it learns one in its weights. All code is available at https://github.com/ArcheOne-AI/RoboScript

papers.title: PACE-ECG: Patient-Aware Contrastive ECG Pretraining; Leveraging Longitudinal Structure for Transferable Representations
papers.abstract_en: Foundation models for physiological signals are commonly evaluated on in-domain interpretation tasks, but their ability to transfer to longitudinal clinical prognosis across healthcare systems remains uncertain. We developed PACE-ECG, an ECG pretraining framework that combines contrastive learning across temporally neighbouring recordings from the same patient with clinically guided multitask supervision. We evaluated frozen ECG representations for post-myocardial-infarction all-cause mortality and incident heart failure prediction across MIMIC-IV and two external HEEDB cohorts, comparing the proposed representation with DeepECG-SSL, a state-of-the-art model, and two control baselines. Across both downstream tasks, the proposed model outperformed DeepECG-SSL in-domain (AUROC +1.9% for mortality and +4.0% for heart failure) and on external populations in HEEDB-Boston (+5.6% for mortality +10.3% for heart failure) and HEEDB-Atlanta (+6.9% for mortality +11.0% for heart failure) while using an encoder 41 times smaller and a fraction of the pretraining data. A matched ablation showed that patient-temporal pairing improved external mortality and heart failure AUROC over generic self-supervision by 7.0% and 9.4% on HEEDB-Boston and 8.9% and 9.3% on HEEDB-Atlanta. These findings indicate that pretraining-objective design greatly influences downstream transfer alongside model and data scale, and that in-domain performance alone is insufficient to establish the clinical generalisability of ECG foundation representations.

papers.title: Breakdown of Autoregressive Multi-Step Reasoning Under Concentrated vs. Diffuse Attention Head Dropout
papers.abstract_en: During extended wakefulness, mammalian neocortical networks experience localized periods of transient neuronal silence termed off-states. Here, we examine how analogous spatiotemporally concentrated disruptions affect sequential reasoning in autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs). Evaluating 250 paired derivations on the GSM8K benchmark across two 8B models (Qwen3-8B and LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct), we contrast clustered bursts of attention head masking against budget-matched diffuse i.i.d. dropout. Concentrated bursts induce substantial reasoning degradation: at onset parameter $\mathcal{B}=0.10$ (scheduling $\sim 5.7\%$ of vulnerable head-token volume), Qwen3-8B accuracy drops from $91.2\%$ under diffuse noise to $78.8\%$ under burst dropout ($Δ= -12.4$ percentage points [pp], exact McNemar $p = 5.5 \times 10^{-6}$), while LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct drops from $84.0\%$ to $76.8\%$ ($Δ= -7.2$ pp, $p = 0.0198$). Conversely, dispersing the identical cumulative budget uniformly across generation steps via stratified quintile matching yields substantially milder degradation (retaining $91.2\%$ in Qwen and $84.0\%$ in LLaMA). In an exploratory factorial dissociation ($N=100$), single-step dropout density is associated with an acute drop in a single schedule draw ($-10.0$ pp on Qwen, $p_{\text{holm}} = 0.0425$), while multi-token continuity exhibits an inconclusive compounding trend ($-7.0$ pp, $p_{\text{holm}} = 0.1892$). Error analysis reveals that Qwen failures reflect derivation errors within formatted responses (conditional accuracy drop of $-11.4$ pp), whereas in LLaMA $22.2\%$ of discordant losses lack a final answer format line (conditional gap narrows to $-5.0$ pp). These findings demonstrate that autoregressive reasoning chains are particularly vulnerable to concentrated structural disruptions, providing empirical benchmarks for fault tolerance in transformer architectures.
